comment: The financing options are well chosen but the guidance does not say who sets the price, on what basis, or with what oversight. Cost recovery and use-based contributions both require a method for determining allowed cost; without one the arrangement is renegotiated annually, which reproduces the instability that recurrent financing is meant to remove.

public.text: The financing options are well chosen but the guidance does not say who sets the price, on what basis, or with what oversight. Cost recovery and use-based contributions both require a method for determining allowed cost; without one the arrangement is renegotiated annually, which reproduces the instability that recurrent financing is meant to remove.
public.suggestedRevision: Add guidance on tariff design for shared digital infrastructure: a statutory basis for the tariff; an independent body that sets it; cost orientation with an approved and capped investment envelope rather than a return on a regulated asset base, which suits physical networks but not fast-depreciating software; short regulatory periods of two to three years with an efficiency benchmark; and service levels attached to the tariff. Note that the cost-recovery model used for generic government digital services in several countries - billing affiliated organisations against an approved multi-year plan - is a closer precedent than utility regulation.
